card: Adds a GitHub Actions CI workflow that produces release packages with Guix for Linux, Windows, and macOS, and runs unit and functional tests on the resulting binaries using native runners. Currently, exact Guix release binaries and their codesigning environments are not continuously tested in CI, leaving packaging and toolchain breakages undetected until release engineering. The workflow checks codesigning environments and generates test harness configurations on the fly to test extracted binaries directly.
changed_since_previous: Added handling in the test runner script to generate `with_sanitizer_env.py` from its template to accommodate changes from merged PR #36308 when running tests against an unpacked release archive.
evidence: PR description: "Currently there is limited continuous testing of our exact release binaries... Many PRs also see Guix builds, although few of those probably run tests against the Guix-built binaries."

PR description: "...in the event that we start shipping some fully-static Linux builds (x64 and aarch64) as per current revision of #25573, our entire custom-built static glibc and compiler toolchain would be relatively untested by current CI jobs, and that would also be tested here."
problem: Release packages produced with Guix are not tested continuously in CI, leaving broken Guix environment manifests, codesign dependencies, and compiler/toolchain-specific bugs unnoticed until manual builds or release time.

risk.why: CI workflows and test harness scripts change only test automation and build-time inspection without altering production binaries or consensus code.

scope_notes: Adds a standalone GitHub Actions workflow file along with helper scripts to install Guix and execute tests against extracted release archives.
summary: Adds a GitHub Actions CI workflow that builds Bitcoin Core via Guix for Linux, Windows, and macOS, then runs unit and functional tests on the produced binaries across native runners. It verifies codesign environments prior to building, exports Guix time-machine metadata for cache re-use, and generates required test-runner config and sanitizer wrappers for unpacked release archives.
